newsitem.title: USA: Looming foreign crude onslaught deadens US crudes.
newsitem.headline: Looming foreign crude onslaught deadens US crudes.

text.p: Outright U.S. crude prices ended a bearish week in fitting fashion, selling-off in the paper markets Friday afternoon after technical support fell at the 19.00 a barrel mark for the prompt month.

Both paper and cash markets were depressed by fundamental oversupply, with cash traders waiting for an onslaught of foreign crude, notably from the North Sea where Shell was heard offering Brent into the U.S. Gulf.
"You've got Dutch/Shell sitting there with 1 million barrels outside the LOOP (Louisiana Offshore Oil Port), you've got Mars kicking in and a lot of crude," said a cash dealer.
